==Problem==
On Monday, Taye has <imath>\$2</imath>. Every day, he either gains <imath>\$3</imath> or doubles the amount of money he had on the previous day. How many different dollar amounts could Taye have on Thursday, <imath>3</imath> days later?

<imath>\textbf{(A) } 3\qquad\textbf{(B) } 4\qquad\textbf{(C) } 5\qquad\textbf{(D) } 6\qquad\textbf{(E) } 7</imath>

==Solution 1 ==
How many dollar values could be on the first day? Only <imath>2</imath> dollars. The second day, you can either add <imath>3</imath> dollars, or double, so you can have <imath>5</imath> dollars, or <imath>4</imath>. For each of these values, you have <imath>2</imath> values for each. For <imath>5</imath> dollars, you have <imath>10</imath> dollars or <imath>8</imath>, and for <imath>4</imath> dollars, you have <imath>8</imath> dollars or <imath>7</imath> dollars. Now, you have <imath>2</imath> values for each of these. For <imath>10</imath> dollars, you have <imath>13</imath> dollars or <imath>20</imath>, for <imath>8</imath> dollars, you have <imath>16</imath> dollars or <imath>11</imath>, for <imath>8</imath> dollars, you have <imath>16</imath> dollars or <imath>11</imath>, and for <imath>7</imath> dollars, you have <imath>14</imath> dollars or <imath>10</imath>.

On the final day, there are 11, 11, 16, and 16 repeating, leaving you with <imath>8-2 = \boxed{\textbf{(D)\ 6}}</imath> different values.
 
~ cxsmi (minor formatting edits)

==Solution 2 ==
Continue as in Solution 1 to get <imath>7</imath>, <imath>8</imath>, or <imath>10</imath> dollars by the 2nd day. The only way to get the same dollar amount occurring twice by branching (multiply by <imath>2</imath> or adding <imath>3</imath>) from here is if <imath>7+3=10\cdot 2</imath> or <imath>7+3=8\cdot 2</imath> which both aren't true. Hence our answer is <imath>3\cdot2=\boxed{\textbf{(D)\ 6}}</imath>. 
 
~ Sahan Wijetunga

==Solution 3 (Brute Force)==
Let <imath>a</imath> represent Taye adding <imath>3</imath> dollars and <imath>d</imath> represent Taye doubling his money.
We can list out all the possibilities:
<imath>a</imath> => <imath>a</imath> => <imath>a</imath> = <imath>11</imath>, 
<imath>a</imath> => <imath>a</imath> => <imath>d</imath> = <imath>16</imath>, 
<imath>a</imath> => <imath>d</imath> => <imath>a</imath> = <imath>12</imath>, 
<imath>a</imath> => <imath>d</imath> => <imath>d</imath> = <imath>20</imath>, 
<imath>d</imath> => <imath>a</imath> => <imath>a</imath> = <imath>10</imath>, 
<imath>d</imath> => <imath>a</imath> => <imath>d</imath> = <imath>14</imath>, 
<imath>d</imath> => <imath>d</imath> => <imath>a</imath> = <imath>11</imath>, 
<imath>d</imath> => <imath>d</imath> => <imath>d</imath> = <imath>16</imath>. 
The unique values are <imath>10,11,12,14,16,20</imath>. Thus, our desired answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)\ 6}}</imath>

~Irfans123
